_comment: Mutation scope is LOGIC, never OUTPUT — the rule is written down in CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
§ Adding an ecosystem, and these globs are it in machine form. Mutating a distribution would
ask "would a test notice if the shipped bytes changed", which `make build-check` already answers
absolutely and for free; mutating tests/budgets/ would mutate a measuring tool. mutmut covers the
Python islands via `make mutation-py`; both report a kill rate; the >=85% requirement the scheduled report applies is inline in
internal/release/ci/mutation_report.sh. No job that can block a merge or a release runs them.
